rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: mapping needs, resources and who can help [Thinking]
rows.description: A daughter lists her father's medical visits, daily support needs, siblings' availability and costs. The map shows that weekday mornings are the real gap.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: family meeting to share responsibilities [Action]
rows.description: She calls her brother and aunt, states the tasks and time needed, and asks each to take a part: he handles finances and hospital visits, she handles daily calls and medicines organisation.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: arranging paid help and a routine [Action]
rows.description: They hire a trained attendant for daytime, set a fixed schedule for meals and doctor visits, and use a shared calendar. This reduces daily emergencies during work hours.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: talking to the manager about flexible hours [Action]
rows.description: He explains his situation to his manager and proposes working from home two days a week with a defined output. The clear proposal is accepted, protecting both care and job.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: doing everything alone out of duty [Pitfall]
rows.description: Believing it is her responsibility, a daughter manages all care after work. Within months she is exhausted, makes errors at work and becomes short-tempered with her parents.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: reacting to each crisis as it comes [Pitfall]
rows.description: Without a plan, every fall or hospital visit means rushing out of the office. Repeated last-minute leaves damage his reputation and leave the family with no backup.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.description: The family lists nearby hospitals, emergency contacts, medical records in one folder and a neighbour with a spare key. When a fall happens, the response takes minutes not hours.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: building in rest and respite for the caregiver [Thinking]
rows.description: Recognising her own energy matters, she schedules a weekly evening off and asks the brother to cover it. Sustainable care is planned like a long journey, not a sprint.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing arrangements as health needs change [Revision]
rows.description: After the father's condition worsens, the family reviews and shifts from a daytime attendant to a professional care option, discussing it with the parents and their doctor.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, critical path, forward planning, resource and budget planning

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: involving the parents in decisions about their care [Thinking]
rows.description: Rather than deciding for them, she asks her mother what help she would accept. The mother prefers a morning helper to moving in, and the plan fits her wishes and independence.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, resource and budget planning
